A measure of unemployment that includes workers who are underemployed and those who are only marginally attached to the labor force reached a record high of 17.4 percent in October 2009 (series dates from 1994)—nearly double its level of 8.8 percent in December 2007. Job losses have been spread broadly across most sectors; from the start of the recession through April 2010, the manufacturing sector has lost 2.1 million jobs, and construction payrolls fell by 1.9 million.
